title: Need help figuring out a skincare routine with the stuff I already have! [Routine Help]
text:
Hi skincare addicts! I (29F) have been a lurker in the community for years, but feel very overwhelmed with all the information. It's been a stressful year and really ever since Covid started and I began working from home, I feel like I've let go on having any routine when it comes to skincare. That, however, hasn't stopped me from buying all sorts of skincare products which I then fail to (routinely) use :) So now it has come to me having a ton of stuff without any idea what to use for the issues I have, when to use what, or in what order products should be applied.

I've added a few pictures to illustrate the issues I have with my skin ([https://imgur.com/JxxcbbP](https://imgur.com/JxxcbbP), [https://imgur.com/RFfzT9u](https://imgur.com/RFfzT9u)). My main concerns are:

1. First wrinkles / skin dryness - as I said, I've had a stressful year and I really see it in my face! I've always had a youthful look and not that there's anything wrong with having wrinkles, but they really seem to have appeared almost overnight. The wrinkles are maybe not that visible on the pictures, but there are lines across my forehead and two very visible "angry-face" lines between my eyebrows. I've seen before&after pictures of people here, so I know the wrinkles can be smoothed at least to some extent with the right products?
2. Sebaceous filaments - a classic issue that I've struggled with for many years, of course I used pore strips when I was a teenager, but don't really want to do that anymore. It also seems like while the SF have always been visible on my nose and cheeks, now my pores have seem to become visibly larger overall (e.g. my forehead)?
3. Dark under-eyes - to be honest, I don't think much can be done regarding these except a good sleep routine, it's probably mostly just my face shape?

Current Routine:

* none really :) In the mornings I usually just wash my face and eyes with water. If I'm feeling more up for it, I swipe a cotton pad with REN's Ready Steady Glow Daily AHA Tonic and add either Sunday Riley's C.E.O. Vitamin C Brightening Serum or Glow Recipe's Watermelon Glow Niacinamide Dew Drops.
* In the evenings, I also often don't do anything. If I can be bothered, I'll wash my face with Youth to the People's Kale + Green Tea Superfood Cleanser (I quite recently purchased it and it seems nice but don't really know yet if/how it affects my skin). I also then apply a cream (either Summer Fridays Cloud Dew oil-free gel cream moisturizer or Medik8 r-Retinoate Intense).
* If I wear foundation, I remove it with the Elemis Pro-collagen Cleansing Balm.
* As I live in Northern Europe and work from home, I don't wear SPF most of the year. If I do go outside for longer during summer-time, I apply Supergoop Unseen Sunscreen.

I've will add pictures + list of the skincare products which I currently have in comments. Most are from CultBeauty's advent calendar from 2022 and actually quite a lot of them I haven't even opened (on the second picture). Missing from the pictures is Sunday Riley's C.E.O. Vitamin C Brightening Serum. I would really-really appreciate it if somebody could put together an AM/PM routine of the products I have! I'm usually very good at following instructions, so I think having an exact routine would help me solve the overwhelming/anxious feeling. I'm also open to adding a few things if it seems I'm missing something (but really, can I be missing something haha?)

title: [Routine Help] What are my next steps for my skincare routine?
text:
Hi all! Between a combination of lurking on this forum and a little bit of trial and error, I've gotten my acne under control in the last few months. I first started getting acne about a year ago. I'd never struggled with my skin as a teenager and really had neglected forming any sort of routine until it developed. But now that I have a solid routine (and honestly habit) built, I would like to keep up with the momentum and continue improving and refining my skincare routine. 

I am 25F, with fair, combo skin that is prone to redness and hyperpigmentation. I have a bit of PIH and just a couple individual spots that scarred from my gnarliest pimples. I don't wear any makeup most days. 

CURRENT ROUTINE:
Morning:
- wash with iS Clinical Cleansing Complex (or just water if my skin is feeling sensitive)
- spot treat with LRP Effaclar Duo (and around my period I treat areas that are especially prone to acne)
- LRP Lipikar Balm AP+ Intense Repair Moisturizing Cream
- EltaMD UV Clear Broad-Spectrum SPF 46

Evening:
- iS Clinical Cleansing Complex
- Differin Adapalene (skip if my skin feels sensitive)
- LRP Lipikar Balm AP+

Products that didn't work for me:
- DHC Deep Cleansing Oil for double cleansing (didn't like the user experience)
- LRP Effaclar Medicated Gel Cleanser (too harsh for me for daily use)
- LRP Effaclar Clarifying Solution (increased skin sensitivity with little pay off)
- Pixie Glow Tonic (same problem as LRP Clarifying Solution)
- Neutrogena Hydro Boost Gel-Cream, Fragrance free (not moisturizing enough)
- Summer Fridays Cloud Dew Oil-Free Gel Cream (horrible reaction)
- FAB Pure Skin Face Cleanser (felt filmy)
- FAB Ultra Repair Clean (too heavy)
- A variety of CeraVe, Cetaphil, and Vanicream cleansers and moisturizers that I have since forgotten the names of

***PLEASE HELP ME WITH***
1. Moisturizer - the LRP one works well for me but I HATE how it makes my skin look
2. Gentle products to give my barrier additional love (maybe a soothing toner, niacinamide, etc.) and help keep my skin calm and even throughout the day
3. An active to help target PIH/anti-aging (vitamin C, etc)
4. Really anything that can take my routine to the next level 

And where to place any suggested products within my routine!

Price isn't a major concern, but I want the value of the product to match what it delivers. (And nothing too absurdly expensive! Lol)

If you made it through this whole post, thank you so much!! I have already learned so much on here but when it comes to making routine decisions, there are so many choices and paths that it makes it feel ime sometimes.
